answer: AI-agent economies can deter Sybil attacks using concurrent memory-hard proof of work. At each epoch, a public beacon seeds a fresh puzzle bound to each agent's key, so hollow replicas cannot echo a peer's proof, and solutions must arrive within a tight time horizon to prevent sequential hardware reuse. This forces attackers to provision dedicated DRAM bandwidth and energy per active identity. Still, large datacenter operators enjoy lower unit costs and can outspend honest edge agents.
